question: After fertilisation in plants, the ovule gets converted into:
solution:
The correct answer is **__Seed.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After fertilization in plants, the ovule gets converted into a seed.
 
• The involves several changes:
 
 
• the fertilized egg within the ovule develops into an embryo,
 
• the ovule itself forms a seed coat, and
 
• the surrounding ovary tissue typically develops into a fruit.
 
 
 
• This transformation is crucial for the plant's reproductive cycle.
 
• Within the ovule, the zygote forms an embryo and integuments become the seed coat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The zygote is the initial cell formed when **two gamete cells (sperm and egg) **are fused during fertilization.
 
• The zygote is a **diploid cell, **meaning it has two sets of chromosomes—one from the male gamete (sperm) and one from the female gamete (egg).
 
• The zygote undergoes its first mitotic division to form a **two-celled embryo.** The division is asymmetric, resulting in two cells of different sizes: **a smaller apical cell and a larger basal cell.**
 
• An **embryo** is a stage of development in multicellular offspring that follows fertilization and occurs before birth or hatching. 
 
• In humans, the embryonic stage spans from the time of fertilization, up to the **end of the 8th week** of pregnancy.
 
• During this period, the foundations for all major organs and body systems are established through a series of complex developmental processes.
